title: Chapter 8. Vasu Ghosha: the Gaura Avatara and Gaura's Form, the Lord's Kirtana and Bhavas in Navadvipa
html:
Padas of Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha known from the Padakalpataru (PK), in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura avatara and His qualities; Gaura's form in Nadia; the Lord's dance and kirtana with the devotees on the bank of the Ganga; the Lord in Radha's mood — gaura-chandrikas to the sections of PK on Radha's states of love (prema-vaichittya, vasaka-sajja, khandita, mana). Majumdar regards Vasu Ghosha as an eyewitness of the Navadvipa kirtanas and counts these padas among his padas on the Lord's form and bhava. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus, the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) and the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Vasu Ghosha — "ki kahiba śata śata tuyā abatāra…" (PK 2292)

Praise of the Gaura avatara: of hundreds of incarnations, the poet holds dear Gauranga alone; as Rama built a bridge across the ocean, Gaura made kirtana a bridge to carry across the lame, the dull and the blind; the poet knows neither japa, nor austerity, nor Vedic reasoning, and begs Gauranga to carry him across too. In PK it stands at the end of the 21st pallava. Raga barari.1

কি কহিব শত শত তুয়া অবতার ।
একলা গৌরাঙ্গচাঁদ পরাণ আমার ॥

ki kahiba śata śata tuyā abatāra |
ekalā gaurāṅgacām̐da parāṇa āmāra ||

ki kahiba — what shall I say; śata śata — hundreds and hundreds; tuyā abatāra — Your incarnations; ekalā — alone; gaurāṅga-cām̐da — Gaurangachand; parāṇa āmāra — my life

1.1What shall I say of Your hundreds and hundreds of incarnations?
Gaurangachand alone is my life.

বিষ্ণু-অবতারে তুমি প্রেমের ভিখারী ।
শিব শুক নারদ লইয়া জনা চারি ॥

biṣṇu-abatāre tumi premera bhikhārī |
śiba śuka nārada laiyā janā cāri ||

biṣṇu-abatāre — in the incarnation of Vishnu; tumi — You; premera bhikhārī — a beggar for prema; śiba śuka nārada — Shiva, Shuka, Narada; laiyā — taking; janā cāri — four persons

1.2In the incarnation of Vishnu You are a beggar asking for prema,
taking four with You: Shiva, Shuka, Narada…2

সেতু-বন্ধ কৈলা তুমি রাম-অবতারে ।
এবে সে তোমার যশ ঘুষিবে সংসারে ॥

setu-bandha kailā tumi rāma-abatāre |
ebe se tomāra yaśa ghuṣibe saṃsāre ||

setu-bandha — the bridge across the ocean; kailā tumi — You made; rāma-abatāre — in the incarnation of Rama; ebe se — but now; tomāra yaśa — Your fame; ghuṣibe — will resound; saṃsāre — through the world

1.3In the incarnation of Rama You built the bridge across the ocean —
but now Your fame will resound through all the world.3

কলি-যুগে কীর্ত্তন করিলা সেতু-বন্ধ ।
সুখে পার হউক যত পঙ্গু জড় অন্ধ ॥

kali-yuge kīrttana karilā setu-bandha |
sukhe pāra hauka yata paṅgu jaṛa andha ||

kali-yuge — in the age of Kali; kīrttana — kirtana; karilā setu-bandha — You made into a bridge; sukhe — with ease (happily); pāra hauka — let them cross over; yata — all; paṅgu — the lame; jaṛa — the dull (immobile); andha — the blind

1.4In the age of Kali You made kirtana the bridge:
let all the lame, the dull and the blind cross over with ease.4

কিবা গুণে পুরুষ নাচে কিবা গুণে নারী ।
গোরা-গুণে মাতিল ভুবন দশ চারি ॥

kibā guṇe puruṣa nāce kibā guṇe nārī |
gorā-guṇe mātila bhubana daśa cāri ||

kibā guṇe — by what qualities; puruṣa nāce — men dance; kibā guṇe nārī — by what qualities women; gorā-guṇe — by Gora's qualities; mātila — are intoxicated; bhubana daśa cāri — the fourteen worlds

1.5By what qualities do men dance, by what qualities women?
By Gora's qualities the fourteen worlds are intoxicated.5

না জানিয়ে জপ তপ এ বেদ-বিচার ।
কহে বাসু গৌরাঙ্গ মোরে কর পার ॥

nā jāniye japa tapa e beda-bicāra |
kahe bāsu gaurāṅga more kara pāra ||

nā jāniye — I do not know; japa tapa — japa, austerity; e beda-bicāra — this Vedic reasoning; kahe bāsu — says Vasu; gaurāṅga — Gauranga; more kara pāra — carry me across

1.6I know neither japa, nor austerity, nor this Vedic reasoning.
Says Vasu: "Gauranga, carry me across!"

barari; MS P-R-Sa no. 2396. GPT1 — p. 46, no. 67 (raga barari); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 67. The catalogue listed the pada twice: under PK 2294 (wrongly: PK 2294 is a pada of Atmarama Dasa on Nityananda, "āre mora nitāi nāyara") and under PK 2292. Majumdar counts PK 2292 among Vasu Ghosha's stavas and prarthanas. a devotee — a "beggar" asking for prema — together with the greatest bhaktas: Shiva, Shuka, Narada (and presumably Brahma; "janā cāri" — "four," or simply "a handful of people"). The Gaudiya tradition sees in Gaura's associates incarnations of these bhaktas (Advaita — Shiva, Srivasa — Narada; GGD). (yata); "kha": "let them cross over now."

2. Vasu Ghosha — "nā jāni ki jāni mora bhela…" (PK 2210)

Praise of Gaura's qualities: remembering them, trees and creepers weep, the forest deities, beasts and birds weep, stones melt, no one can stay at home; the poet loses himself. In PK it stands in the 20th pallava ("Sri Gaurachandra — another mode"). Raga suhai.6

না জানি কি জানি মোর ভেল ।
ভাবিতে গৌরাঙ্গ-গুণ তনু মোর গেল ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nā jāni ki jāni mora bhela |
bhābite gaurāṅga-guṇa tanu mora gela || dhru ||

nā jāni — I do not know; ki jāni — what indeed; mora bhela — has happened to me; bhābite — thinking of; gaurāṅga-guṇa — Gauranga's qualities; tanu mora gela — my body is gone (I forgot my body)

2.1(Refrain) I do not know what has happened to me:
thinking of Gauranga's qualities, I have forgotten my body.

গোরা-গুণ সোঙরিয়া কান্দে বৃক্ষ লতা ।
গুণ সোঙরিয়া কান্দে বনের দেবতা ॥

gorā-guṇa soṅariyā kānde bṛkṣa latā |
guṇa soṅariyā kānde banera debatā ||

gorā-guṇa — Gora's qualities; soṅariyā — remembering; kānde bṛkṣa latā — trees and creepers weep; guṇa soṅariyā — remembering the qualities; kānde banera debatā — the deities of the forest weep

2.2Remembering Gora's qualities, the trees and creepers weep;
remembering His qualities, the deities of the forest weep.7

গোরা-গুণ সোঙরিয়া গলয়ে পাথরে ।
গুণ সোঙরিয়া কেহো নাহি রহে ঘরে ॥

gorā-guṇa soṅariyā galaye pāthare |
guṇa soṅariyā keho nāhi rahe ghare ||

gorā-guṇa soṅariyā — remembering Gora's qualities; galaye pāthare — the stones melt; guṇa soṅariyā — remembering the qualities; keho nāhi rahe ghare — no one stays at home

2.3Remembering Gora's qualities, the stones melt;
remembering His qualities, no one stays at home.

বাসুদেব ঘোষ গুণ সোঙরিয়া কান্দে ।
পশু পাখী কান্দে গুণে স্থির নাহি বান্ধে ॥

bāsudeba ghoṣa guṇa soṅariyā kānde |
paśu pākhī kānde guṇe sthira nāhi bāndhe ||

bāsudeba ghoṣa — Vasudeva Ghosha; guṇa soṅariyā kānde — weeps remembering the qualities; paśu pākhī kānde — beasts and birds weep; guṇe — at the qualities; sthira nāhi bāndhe — find no rest

2.4Vasudeva Ghosha weeps, remembering His qualities;
at His qualities beasts and birds weep, finding no rest.

3. Vasu Ghosha — "gorā-guṇa gāo gāo śuni…" (PK 2185)

Praise of Gaura: the poet asks that His qualities be sung; the Lord is the touchstone of prema; a single glance of His dries up the ocean of grief of all souls; His eyes are full of tears, His words are engraved on the heart, His body is covered with the thrill of ecstasy. In PK it stands in the 20th pallava. Raga mallar.8

গোরা-গুণ গাও গাও শুনি ।
অনেক পুণ্যের ফলে সো পহু মিলায়ল
প্রেম-পরশ-রস-মণি ॥ ধ্রু ॥

gorā-guṇa gāo gāo śuni |
aneka puṇyera phale so pahu milāyala
prema-paraśa-rasa-maṇi || dhru ||

gorā-guṇa — of Gora's qualities; gāo gāo — sing, sing; śuni — let me hear; aneka puṇyera phale — by the fruit of many pious deeds; so pahu — that Lord; milāyala — has been brought (revealed to us); prema-paraśa-rasa-maṇi — the touchstone of the rasa of prema

3.1(Refrain) Sing, sing of Gora's qualities — let me hear!
By the fruit of many pious deeds that Lord has been revealed to us —
the touchstone of the rasa of prema.9

অখিল জীবের এ শোক-সায়র
শোষয়ে নয়ান-নিমিখে ।
ও প্রেম-লবলেশ পরশ না পাইলে
পরাণ জুড়াইবে কিসে ॥

akhila jībera e śoka-sāyara
śoṣaye nayāna-nimikhe |
o prema-labaleśa paraśa nā pāile
parāṇa juṛāibe kise ||

akhila jībera — of all souls; e śoka-sāyara — this ocean of grief; śoṣaye — He dries up; nayāna-nimikhe — in the blink of an eye; o prema-laba-leśa — even a drop of that prema; paraśa nā pāile — without touching; parāṇa juṛāibe kise — with what will the heart be cooled

3.2This ocean of grief of all souls
He dries up in the blink of an eye.
Without the touch of even a drop of that prema,
with what will you cool your heart?

অরুণ নয়ান বরুণ-আলয়
করুণাময় নিরখণে ।
মধুর আলাপনে আখরে আখরে
পাঁজরে পাতিয়া লিখনে ॥

aruṇa nayāna baruṇa-ālaya
karuṇāmaya nirakhaṇe |
madhura ālāpane ākhare ākhare
pām̐jare pātiyā likhane ||

aruṇa nayāna — reddish eyes; baruṇa-ālaya — the abode of Varuna; karuṇāmaya — of the Merciful One; nirakhaṇe — in gazing; madhura ālāpane — in sweet talk; ākhare ākhare — syllable by syllable; pām̐jare pātiyā — laid out upon the ribs; likhane — written

3.3His reddish eyes are the abode of Varuna
when the Merciful One gazes;
in His sweet talk every word
is as if written into the heart.10

প্রেমে ঢল ঢল পুলকে পূরল
আপাদমস্তক তনু ।
বাসুদেব কহে সহস্র-ধারা বহে
সুমেরু সিঞ্চিত জনু ॥

preme ḍhala ḍhala pulake pūrala
āpādamastaka tanu |
bāsudeba kahe sahasra-dhārā bahe
sumeru siñcita janu ||

preme ḍhala ḍhala — swaying in prema; pulake pūrala — filled with the thrill of ecstasy; āpādamastaka tanu — the body from foot to head; bāsudeba kahe — says Vasudeva; sahasra-dhārā bahe — a thousand streams flow; sumeru siñcita janu — as if Sumeru were being bathed

3.4He sways in prema; the thrill of ecstasy
fills His body from head to foot.
Says Vasudeva: a thousand streams are flowing —
as if Sumeru were being bathed.11

Majumdar counts PK 2185 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. lit. "written, laid out upon the ribs" (pām̐jare pātiyā likhane). 4. Vasu Ghosha — "cīta-cora gaura mora…" (PK 341)

Gaura's form: the stealer of hearts, intoxicated with prema, embraces the destitute and the fallen; His name is the cause of the deliverance of the worlds; for the sake of souls He left His abode and appeared in Nadia like the autumn moon; the Creator fashioned Him an ocean of rasa; seeing Him, all sorrow departs. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika at the beginning of the 6th pallava (abhisarikas of the rainy season, etc.). Raga tori.12

চীত-চোর গৌর মোর
প্রেমে মত্ত মগন ভোর
অকিঞ্চন জনে করই কোর
পতিত-অধম-বন্ধুয়া ।

cīta-cora gaura mora
preme matta magana bhora
akiñcana jane karai kora
patita-adhama-bandhuyā |

cīta-cora — the stealer of hearts; gaura mora — my Gaura; preme matta — intoxicated with prema; magana bhora — immersed, enraptured; akiñcana jane — the destitute; karai kora — takes in His embrace; patita-adhama-bandhuyā — the friend of the fallen and the low

4.1The stealer of hearts is my Gaura,
intoxicated with prema, immersed, enraptured;
the destitute He takes in His embrace —
the friend of the fallen and the low.

ভুবন-তারণ-কারণ নাম
জীব লাগিয়া তেজল ধাম
প্রকট হইলা নদিয়া নগরে
যৈছে শরদ-ইন্দুয়া ॥

bhubana-tāraṇa-kāraṇa nāma
jība lāgiyā tejala dhāma
prakaṭa hailā nadiyā nagare
yaiche śarada-induyā ||

bhubana-tāraṇa-kāraṇa nāma — the name that is the cause of the deliverance of the worlds; jība lāgiyā — for the sake of souls; tejala dhāma — left His abode; prakaṭa hailā — appeared; nadiyā nagare — in the town of Nadia; yaiche śarada-induyā — like the autumn moon

4.2His name is the cause of the deliverance of the worlds;
for the sake of souls He left His abode
and appeared in the town of Nadia
like the autumn moon.13

অসীম মহিমা কে করু ওর
যুবতি-জীবন করই চোর
বিধি নিরমিল কি দিয়া গৌর
বড়ই রসের সিন্ধুয়া ।

asīma mahimā ke karu ora
yubati-jībana karai cora
bidhi niramila ki diyā gaura
baṛai rasera sindhuyā |

asīma mahimā — boundless glory; ke karu ora — who can find the limit; yubati-jībana — the life of young women; karai cora — steals; bidhi niramila — the Creator fashioned; ki diyā — from what; gaura — Gaura; baṛai rasera sindhuyā — a vast ocean of rasa

4.3Who can find the limit of His boundless glory?
He steals the very life of young women.
From what did the Creator fashion Gaura —
a vast ocean of rasa?14

দেখিতে দেখিতে লাগয়ে সুখ
হরল সকল মনের দুখ
বাসুঘোষ কহে কিবা সে রূপ
নিরখি চিত সানন্দুয়া ॥

dekhite dekhite lāgaye sukha
harala sakala manera dukha
bāsughoṣa kahe kibā se rūpa
nirakhi cita sānanduyā ||

dekhite dekhite — looking and looking; lāgaye sukha — joy arises; harala sakala manera dukha — all the sorrow of the heart is taken away; bāsughoṣa kahe — says Vasu Ghosha; kibā se rūpa — what beauty is this; nirakhi — beholding; cita sānanduyā — the heart is full of bliss

4.4Looking and looking, joy arises,
all the sorrow of the heart is taken away.
Says Vasu Ghosha: what beauty is this!
Beholding it, the heart is full of bliss.

GPT1 — pp. 131–132, no. 60 (raga tori); GPT2 — sect. 3.1, no. 60. Majumdar counts PK 341 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's form. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta).

5. Vasu Ghosha — "dekha dekha gorā naṭa-rāy…" (PK 2143)

The form of Gaura, the king of dancers: His face is the autumn moon with a gentle smile; champaka buds in His curls; golden earrings, lips redder than the bimba; His voice is a wave of nectar drowning the world in the rasa of Hari; His arms are lovelier than an elephant's trunk; His chest is a golden mountain, His navel a lotus lake; He wears crimson cloth, and ankle-bells ring on His feet. In PK it stands in the 18th pallava (the form of Gauranga). Raga gandhara.15

দেখ দেখ গোরা নট-রায় ।
বদন-শরদ-শশী তাহে মন্দ মন্দ হাসি
কুলবতী হেরি মুরছায় ॥

dekha dekha gorā naṭa-rāya |
badana-śarada-śaśī tāhe manda manda hāsi
kulabatī heri murachāya ||

dekha dekha — behold, behold; gorā naṭa-rāy — Gora, king of dancers; badana-śarada-śaśī — the face, an autumn moon; tāhe — on it; manda manda hāsi — a gentle, gentle smile; kulabatī — chaste women; heri — seeing; murachāy — swoon

5.1Behold, behold Gora, the king of dancers!
His face is the autumn moon, and on it a gentle, gentle smile;
seeing it, chaste women swoon.16

চাঁচর চিকুর মাথে চম্পক-কলিকা তাথে
যুবতীর মন মধুকর ।
শ্রুতি-পদ্মযুগ-মূলে কনক-কুণ্ডল দোলে
পাকা বিম্বু জিনিয়া অধর ॥

cām̐cara cikura māthe campaka-kalikā tāthe
yubatīra mana madhukara |
śruti-padmayuga-mūle kanaka-kuṇḍala dole
pākā bimbu jiniyā adhara ||

cām̐cara cikura māthe — curling locks on the head; campaka-kalikā tāthe — champaka buds in them; yubatīra mana madhukara — the hearts of young women are bees; śruti-padmayuga-mūle — at the roots of the two lotus ears; kanaka-kuṇḍala dole — golden earrings sway; pākā bimbu jiniyā — surpassing the ripe bimba; adhara — the lips

5.2On His head, curling locks, and in them champaka buds —
and the bee-hearts of young women.
At the roots of His lotus ears golden earrings sway;
His lips surpass the ripe bimba fruit.17

কম্বু কণ্ঠে মৃদু বাণী সুধার তরঙ্গ খানি
হরি-রসে জগত ডুবায় ।
করিবর-কর জিনি বাহু-যুগ সুবলনি
অঙ্গদ বলয়া শোভে তায় ॥

kambu kaṇṭhe mṛdu bāṇī sudhāra taraṅga khāni
hari-rase jagata ḍubāya |
karibara-kara jini bāhu-yuga subalani
aṅgada balayā śobhe tāya ||

kambu kaṇṭhe — from the conch-like throat; mṛdu bāṇī — soft words; sudhāra taraṅga khāni — a wave of nectar; hari-rase — in the rasa of Hari; jagata ḍubāy — drowns the world; karibara-kara jini — surpassing the trunk of a mighty elephant; bāhu-yuga subalani — the two rounded arms; aṅgada balayā — armlets and bracelets; śobhe tāy — shine on them

5.3From His conch-like throat come soft words, a wave of nectar
that drowns the world in the rasa of Hari.
Surpassing the trunk of a mighty elephant are His two rounded arms,

The Lord in Radha's mood — mana: Gora weeps, repeating "Krishna, Krishna," tears flow from His eyes like Gangas; He does not anoint His body with sandal, and, all grey with dust, rolls on the ground; His face is dulled with pique, nothing pleases Him, neither by day nor by night does He sleep.
